i was transferred here from the another campus' er because they thought i had the coronavirus and this is where they were sending covid-19 patients to consolidate them at one location.  i didn't think i had it - they just said my symptoms were likely to be covid-19 - i had one symptom, shortness of breath and valley fever scarred lungs - that combination apparently got me the golden ticket to get shipped on over to abrazo central campus.

i got there around 1pm, got one set of vitals, and was told by the nurse that they wouldn't come in, if you needed anything to call.  i talked to a doctor on the phone who said i probably didn't have covid-19 but they needed to wait for the results of the test.  so for several hours i was left alone until the night shift nurse came on (when i finally got a gown and a blanket).  she at least came in several times to check vitals during the night - got woken up in the middle of the night to get a second covid-19 test since they could not find the first one.  

the next day, surprise!, i don't have covid-19 and they are going to move me from the covid-19 section to another room.  i get a cardiologist who basically tells me i am ok to go home even though i am still having some shortness of breath @7am (also absolutely nothing had been done at this point since everyone was waiting for the results of that test).  they move me to another room on another floor @10am where the bathroom floor is always wet because the shower is leaking (where they give me toiletries finally - luckily i had someone drop off my phone charger, toothbrush and toothpaste, etc the day before so i didn't need anything).  

i am pretty much ignored for several more hours - i got an echo (the technician who did the test was awesome at least) and then "you are going home" @5pm (without talking to a doctor about what the echo showed or any information).  i asked to speak to a doctor and he came and really didn't explain much and just said that i could come see him and get another test done at his office - and at that point i was really ready to get out of there and go home and see my own doctor anyway.

granted, i do understand some of this because of the covid-19 virus going around, but even when i was moved to a regular floor, i couldn't get answers and i got discharged with a shortness of breath diagnosis and a diet plan.  i asked for the echo results to give to my regular cardiologist and was told that i couldn't have them because they hadn't been read yet

the nurses were nice enough when you saw one ...
and the food was not bad (except for the turkey sausage - don't ever get the turkey sausage) but i really hope not to return to this location especially not during the pandemic, but probably not ever

i am pretty sure i am going to be getting a big bill for basically getting misdiagnosed and ignored - can't wait to see the cost of that!
